metadata.question: Did the turbidity of the Beaufort Sea (specifically at 69.954148, -136.325766) increase between June 14, 2012, and July 5, 2012?

data.raw_code: The user asks: "Did the turbidity of the Beaufort Sea (specifically at 69.954148, -136.325766) increase between June 14, 2012, and July 5, 2012?" We need to: 1. Define the geometry (point at given coordinates). 2. Define two time periods: around June 14, 2012 and around July 5, 2012. We should use a small date window (e.g., ±3 days) to get cloud-free imagery. 3. Choose a satellite collection that measures turbidity. For water quality, common options are: - Landsat 7 (available in 2012) but has SLC-off issues after 2003. - Landsat 5 (available until 2013) but might have data gaps. - MODIS (daily data) but lower spatial resolution. - Sentinel-2 started in 2015, so not available for 2012. Best option: Landsat 5 Surface Reflectance Tier 1 (LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2) which has bands for water quality analysis. We can use the SWIR1 band (Band 5) or NIR band (Band 4) as a proxy for turbidity. Alternatively, we can use the Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) = (Red - Green)/(Red + Green) using bands 3 and 2. Actually, for Landsat 5: - Band 2: Green (0.52-0.60 µm) - Band 3: Red (0.63-0.69 µm) We can compute NDTI = (B3 - B2) / (B3 + B2). Higher values indicate higher turbidity. 4. We need to: - Filter collections for each date window. - Apply cloud masking (using QA_PIXEL band for Landsat 5). - Calculate NDTI for each image. - Compute mean NDTI in a buffer around the point. - Compare the two values. 5. Check for no data (C1), no valid pixels (C2), or calculation failure (C3). 6. Output concise evidence and final answer tag. Let me structure the code: 1. Geometry: Point at (69.954148, -136.325766) and create a buffer (e.g., 1000m) for region reduction. 2. Date windows: - Period1: June 11 to June 17, 2012 (around June 14) - Period2: July 2 to July 8, 2012 (around July 5) 3. Collection: Landsat 5 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance. 4. Cloud masking: Use QA_PIXEL band to mask clouds and cloud shadow (bits 3 and 4). 5. Calculate NDTI: (B3 - B2) / (B3 + B2). 6. For each period: - Check if collection has images. - If empty, try fallback (maybe MODIS or wider date window). - Compute median composite (or best image) and calculate mean NDTI in buffer. - Check pixel count. 7. Compare mean NDTI values: if July 5 > June 14, then answer "A: Yes", else "B: No". We must handle cases: - C1: No images in one or both periods. - C2: Images exist but no valid pixels after masking. - C3: Calculation yields NaN or unreasonable values. Also note: Landsat 5 has 30m resolution. We'll use scale=1000 for reduceRegion to avoid memory issues. Let me write the code accordingly. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Define geometry and date windows const point = ee.Geometry.Point([-136.325766, 69.954148]); const region = point.buffer(1000); // 1km buffer for reduction const juneWindow = ee.DateRange('2012-06-11', '2012-06-17'); const julyWindow = ee.DateRange('2012-07-02', '2012-07-08'); // Function to mask clouds and shadows in Landsat 5 function maskL5sr(image) { const qaMask = image.select('QA_PIXEL').bitwiseAnd(parseInt('1111', 2)).eq(0); const saturationMask = image.select('QA_RADSAT').eq(0); return image.updateMask(qaMask).updateMask(saturationMask); } // Function to calculate NDTI (Normalized Difference Turbidity Index) function addNDTI(image) { const ndti = image.normalizedDifference(['SR_B3', 'SR_B2']).rename('NDTI'); return image.addBands(ndti); } // 2. Get Landsat 5 collections for both periods let juneCol = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2') .filterBounds(point) .filterDate(juneWindow) .map(maskL5sr) .map(addNDTI); let julyCol = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2') .filterBounds(point) .filterDate(julyWindow) .map(maskL5sr) .map(addNDTI); // Check collection sizes const juneSize = juneCol.size().getInfo(); const julySize = julyCol.size().getInfo(); console.log(`June 14 window images: ${juneSize}`); console.log(`July 5 window images: ${julySize}`); // 3. Handle empty collections - try wider date windows if needed if (juneSize === 0 || julySize === 0) { // Try widening the date window by ±7 days console.log('One collection empty, trying wider date window (±7 days)...'); juneCol = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2') .filterBounds(point) .filterDate('2012-06-07', '2012-06-21') .map(maskL5sr) .map(addNDTI); julyCol = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2') .filterBounds(point) .filterDate('2012-06-28', '2012-07-12') .map(maskL5sr) .map(addNDTI); const juneSizeWide = juneCol.size().getInfo(); const julySizeWide = julyCol.size().getInfo(); console.log(`June wide window images: ${juneSizeWide}`); console.log(`July wide window images: ${julySizeWide}`); if (juneSizeWide === 0 || julySizeWide === 0) { console.log('C1'); return; } } // 4. Create median composites and compute mean NDTI const juneImg = juneCol.median(); const julyImg = julyCol.median(); // Function to compute statistics function getStats(img, periodName) { const stats = img.select('NDTI').reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean().combine({ reducer2: ee.Reducer.count(), sharedInputs: true }), geometry: region, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9, bestEffort: true }); const mean = stats.get('NDTI_mean'); const count = stats.get('NDTI_count'); return {mean: mean, count: count}; } const juneStats = getStats(juneImg, 'June'); const julyStats = getStats(julyImg, 'July'); // 5. Check for valid pixels const juneCount = juneStats.count.getInfo(); const julyCount = julyStats.count.getInfo(); console.log(`June valid pixels: ${juneCount}`); console.log(`July valid pixels: ${julyCount}`); if (juneCount === 0 || julyCount === 0) { console.log('C2'); return; } // 6. Get mean values and validate const juneMean = juneStats.mean.getInfo(); const julyMean = julyStats.mean.getInfo(); console.log(`June mean NDTI: ${juneMean !== null ? juneMean.toFixed(4) : 'null'}`); console.log(`July mean NDTI: ${julyMean !== null ? julyMean.toFixed(4) : 'null'}`); // Validate results if (juneMean === null || julyMean === null || isNaN(juneMean) || isNaN(julyMean) || juneMean < -1 || juneMean > 1 || julyMean < -1 || julyMean > 1) { console.log('C3'); return; } // 7. Compare and output answer if (julyMean > juneMean) { console.log('A'); } else { console.log('B'); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
